symptoms: 1-month history of hyperpigmentation of the oral mucosa
physical_exam: Multiple coalescing painless nonpruritic black macules and patches on the tongue, roof of the mouth, and buccal mucosa
Erythematous and hyperpigmented patches covering 90% of the body surface area
1- to 2-cm lymphadenopathy in the bilateral inguinal folds and axillae

diagnostic_test.name: Clinical Examination
findings: Hyperpigmentation of the oral mucosa with coalescing black macules and patches
Widespread erythematous and hyperpigmented skin patches

branch.interpretation: Evaluate differential diagnoses for oral hyperpigmentation in a patient with known mycosis fungoides.
branch.result: Findings and patient history favor the diagnosis of oral involvement of mycosis fungoides.

diagnostic_options.description: A benign condition characterized by mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation, typically without systemic involvement.
A malignancy that presents as pigmented lesions which could theoretically involve the oral mucosa.
evidence_against: Lesion distribution is diffuse and correlates with existing mycosis fungoides
No classic melanoma features or solitary lesion presentation

diagnostic_options.description: Some medications can induce hyperpigmentation; however, the pattern is inconsistent with drug-induced changes.
evidence_against: Temporal profile and progression do not match medication-induced pigmentation
Patient had partial response to therapies rather than new drug exposure causing pigmentation

diagnostic_options.description: The extension of cutaneous lymphoma to the oral mucosa, consistent with the patient’s history and clinical presentation.
evidence_for: Known history of mycosis fungoides with extensive skin involvement
Lymphadenopathy and systemic signs support disease progression

conclusion: The most likely diagnosis is oral involvement of mycosis fungoides.
